name: manual_4fae81
claim: Make a shell-safety hook table-driven: each rule is data (id, level, hint) with bad and good fixtures that a self-test and the tests execute; rules that guess at runtime state only warn; a rollout starts in warn mode with a log of rule ids and a command hash, never the command text; the installer defaults to a read-only check, validates settings before changing anything, backs them up and merges without clobbering. Generate the rule table in the docs from the registry and test that it matches.

decisions.notes: A hook for zsh and macOS traps was reviewed by three agents. Fixtures caught two pattern bugs on the first run, the generated-table test caught a stale doc after rules were demoted, the installer test caught files being copied before an invalid settings file was detected, and a side note showed an unmatched-glob rule would block a command that creates the files first.

rationale: A hook for zsh and macOS traps was reviewed by three agents. Fixtures caught two pattern bugs on the first run, the generated-table test caught a stale doc after rules were demoted, the installer test caught files being copied before an invalid settings file was detected, and a side note showed an unmatched-glob rule would block a command that creates the files first.
